title: Ginger and Matcha Granita
changes_from_base: Green tea steeped with crystallised ginger, matcha and honey replaces the strawberry purée; no sugar.
summary: A refreshing frozen treat combining the warmth of crystallised ginger with the earthy notes of matcha and a bright hint of lemon.

steps.title: Infuse
steps.text: Place 720 ml water and 30 g finely chopped crystallised ginger in a saucepan and bring almost to the boil. Add 3 green tea bags, cover with a lid, and remove from the heat to steep for 5 min.

steps.title: Strain
steps.text: Pass the liquid through a fine sieve into a bowl, discarding the tea bags and ginger pieces. Ensure the liquid remains warm enough to dissolve the remaining ingredients.

steps.title: Mix matcha
steps.text: In a small bowl, whisk 1 tsp matcha powder with 2 tbsp of the warm tea to form a smooth paste. Whisk this paste back into the main batch of tea until fully combined.

steps.title: Sweeten
steps.text: Stir in 80 g honey and 2 tbsp lemon juice until dissolved. Taste the mixture to ensure it is fairly sweet, as the flavour dulls slightly once frozen.

steps.title: First freeze
steps.text: Cool the liquid completely before pouring it into a shallow glass or ceramic dish. Place the dish in the freezer.

steps.title: Scrape
steps.text: Every 30 min, stir the mixture with a fork to create slushy crystals. Continue this process for about 3 h until the texture is consistent throughout.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: If the granita sets too hard, leave it in the fridge for 10-15 min. Fork the ice again to restore the light texture before serving.

tips: Use high quality matcha powder for the most vibrant green colour and best flavour.
Ensure you do not over-steep the tea bags to avoid any unwanted bitterness.
Serve in chilled glasses to prevent the delicate ice crystals from melting too quickly.
storage: Keep the granita covered in the freezer for up to 1 week and fork the crystals or soften in the fridge before serving.
